summary: Closed the full remote co-sign loop end-to-end. Five sub-cuts in one session: ε (auto-route inbox to the matching cosign modal), NIP-44 reference-vector verification (10/10 vectors spec-conformant), ζ (Send-back-via-Nostr after the witness signs), η (Send-via-Nostr in CosignRequestModal), θ (peer picker driven from handshake holdings). The whole loop now runs without copy-paste — pick a peer, tap Send, the other side auto-routes and signs back, both wallets converge on the dual-signed envelope. All eight gates green; pushed branch only. Branch is 11 commits ahead of main with the complete 5c-i slice plus the spec interop proof.

why.text: The slice that started with NIP-44 four sessions ago has been threading toward a single goal: two people with a Tier P handshake should be able to co-sign anything later without being in the same room. This session connected the last pipes. The inbox now routes (5c-i-ε), the reply travels (5c-i-ζ), the initiator can pick up the conversation from any journal entry (5c-i-η), and the recipient is one tap from a known connection (5c-i-θ). The NIP-44 reference-vector test (10/10 spec vectors) closes the homework that was on the list since the very first cut.

Total 11 commits ahead of main now: 5c-i α/β/γ/δ/ε/ζ/η/θ plus the NIP-44 interop test plus two comms close-out commits from earlier sessions. All cuts are pure additions, each independently safe.

uncertainty: The remote co-sign loop has been unit-tested end-to-end via fake transport but has not been smoke-tested against real public relays with two real devices. The next operator field test is the first cross-implementation evidence — NIP-44 interop is now verified against spec vectors, so the cryptographic floor is sound, but the wire-protocol behavior against unknown relays still arrives only with use.
